question: Where can resolved numbered or named heights DDS bytes be replaced before parsing, and which buffer-ownership and native byte-transfer conditions apply?

scope.boundary: Selected common file-wrapper return, height creation and source-buffer release, and local resource lock/cleanup bodies. Existing formatter, resolver ordering, DDS parser/upload and CPU-reader contracts are reused. This is a static hook candidate, not runtime acceptance or an allocator-compatibility theorem.
scope.qualification: Require the original save/restore ABI, normal helper return, valid nonalias stack/object/guest storage, retained filename and buffer contents, sufficient backing, and nonwrapping address/size arithmetic. Selected word equality does not prove unqueried child effects, current providers or whole-project identity.

dependencies.use: Both numbered and named base formats converge on the height request through 0x822F9888.
The bare-name common file path attempts direct open, registered sources and then the common fallback.
Height creation and the distinct blend/lightmap type7 cold-file chains.
Classic DDS parsing, local copy, extraction and the BE16 CPU consumer remain separate contracts.
Retail-observed height profile and the still-open native sample-byte transfer; no complete authoring recipe is inferred.
The GFx type11 opener and its common-loader fallback differ from the native height ingress.
The bounded accepted logo override at 0x82E87B90 is a separate ownership and call path.

recommendedHook.position: Immediately after the 0x822D6504 call to 0x82E806E0 returns, before storing its returned allocation base through r31. All locally selected source-return arms converge here before the height parser call.

registers.r1: T, the current wrapper stack pointer
registers.r30: Original NUL-terminated filename pointer, captured from incoming r4
registers.r3: A, the resolved allocation base; zero is a load miss/failure
registers.r31: C, the output-pointer cell captured from incoming r3

recommendedHook.length: For nonnull A with valid prefix storage, L=BE U32[A]. L excludes the four-byte prefix and includes the complete DDS file, including its DDS header.
recommendedHook.data: P=A+4 points to the complete file. The prefix is allocation metadata, not part of the on-disk DDS. Classic DDS sample data begins at P+128.

heightsCallerFilter.binding: The wrapper saves incoming LR at oldSP-8 and allocates a 0x70-byte frame. The height call at 0x822F98B8 sets LR=0x822F98BC. For that caller, C=heightSP+0x94=T+0x104. This return address is unique among the seven enumerated direct wrapper callers; indirect callers remain unknown.

recommendedHook.nameFilter: Combine the saved-height-caller check with a bounded exact match of the actual caller-built filename at r30. Capture that string at runtime before trusting a name filter: its exact prefix, path and case are not fixed here. Do not substitute the higher-level bare role name, assume case folding, use only a suffix, or treat caller identity as a unique map identity. Preserve the A==0 failure path.
recommendedHook.resume: Preserve the frame, saved link, filename, output-cell address and required ABI state. Resume the original store. The nonnull arm subsequently stores P=A+4 to C at 0x822D6514/0x822D6518 and returns P; do not substitute P where this hook expects allocation base A.
recommendedHook.qualification: Both selected direct and stream arms request L+4 storage and construct the same prefix/payload layout. Allocator rounding/effects, complete-read semantics, writable backing and ordinary interface/retention premises remain open.
recommendedHook.corroboration: The selected register, prefix and saved-link tuple is statically corroborated. Runtime hook operation, name-filter identity and writable backing are not established.

requestCoverage.numberedAndNamed: Numbered and named reach rests on map-authoring-loader-boundary.json#/textureLoader: the cited base-format branches construct the height role name and request 0x822F9888. This finding does not independently close the exact caller-built prefix/path/case or observe runtime reach.
requestCoverage.resolvedSources: 0x82E806E0 returns either a direct-opener result or a selected stream/source allocation before the hook. Reuse map-content-precedence.json#/resolverOrder for bare names. Do not generalize that bare-name ordering to a named selector containing path separators.
requestCoverage.sharedLoads: Cold-load qualification applies to the blend/lightmap type7 path through sub_82C8E150, whose cache can bypass this wrapper. It does not describe sub_822F9888, which reaches the wrapper for every nonnull, nonempty name. The wrapper is shared by the direct callers listed below, so a height override must discriminate its caller/name.
requestCoverage.logoComparison: This is not the logo hook 0x82E87B90 in GFx owner 0x82E87B28. The logo's accepted type11 File Data path has a different lifetime. The GFx filesystem fallback joins lower common loader 0x82E806E0, not proof that the native height path reaches the logo instruction.
requestCoverage.heightIngress: Within sub_822F9888 there is no cache lookup or early exit before 0x822F98B8 -> 0x822D64C0 beyond a null or empty incoming name, under the original ABI. Any warm bypass at this immediate call boundary must occur in one of its three direct callers; their behavior is uncharacterized.
requestCoverage.directCensusQualification: Exact generated direct-call enumeration and selected native branch validation bind these seven wrapper callers and three height callers. The wrapper return addresses are distinct. Only indirect callers remain unknown.

heightParserHandoff.postLoad: 0x822F98BC captures P from heightSP+0x94 into r29. That height-local point is after resolution but has no proven ABI-retained filename register or slot; the single wrapper hook retains both name and allocation.
heightParserHandoff.reusedStackCell: At 0x822F98CC, 0x82C988B8 receives the same cell C. It stores zero on its null-global arm, otherwise requests 0x821B3AD8, freshly reloads global 0x82F8E270 and stores global+0xBC to C. File P remains separately in r29. Do not mistake the later C value for file bytes.
heightParserHandoff.creationCall: At 0x822F991C -> 0x8257B8A8, r3=U32[C] is the getter result, r4=P, r5=BE U32[P-4], and r10=0x28000058. 0x822F9914 retains A=P-4 in r26. Other fixed arguments remain the existing role-consumer contract.
heightParserHandoff.qualification: Getter child effects, fresh global validity and retention of r29, C and A remain premises. An argument-only override at the later creation call would need its own ownership/alias analysis; it is not the recommended single-point contract.
heightParserHandoff.callerBuiltName: The higher-level height caller builds the filename through sub_827F2830. This finding does not fix the resulting prefix, path or case at the wrapper. Capture the bounded r30 string for the intended numbered/named request before trusting an exact-name filter.
heightParserHandoff.sizeChecks: After the hook, the only file-size consumer seen in the selected creation handoff is r5=BE U32[P-4], loaded at 0x822F98E0 and passed at 0x822F991C. An equal-size copy with the prefix unchanged satisfies that observed size consumer. Parser internals beyond the selected handoff window were not read for this finding; additional parser-internal size checks are not excluded or closed by this result.

sourceAllocationAndOwnership.streamAllocation: For a nonzero reported size L, 0x82E807E8/0x82E807EC requests low32(L+4) bytes from 0x82D3DBA0. 0x82E807FC writes BE length L at A and requests file bytes into A+4 through the selected 0x82E48590 or 0x82D38448 read helper. A zero read-helper result requests 0x82D3D9F0(A) at 0x82E80840 and returns zero.
sourceAllocationAndOwnership.wrapperOldValue: A preexisting nonzero output P passed to 0x822D64C0 is first sent as P-4 to 0x82D3D9F0, then C is cleared before loading. The ordinary height caller initializes C to zero, so that old-value branch is not selected for this invocation.
sourceAllocationAndOwnership.heightCreationFailure: A nonzero creation result requests release through sub_82D3D9F0 with r3=A at call 0x822F9954, LR 0x822F9958, then returns 0 under ordinary intervening diagnostic/context-helper effects. The release descendants are unqueried.
sourceAllocationAndOwnership.heightSuccess: After selected descriptor/lock/extraction and temporary-resource cleanup, call 0x822F9A58, LR 0x822F9A5C, requests release through sub_82D3D9F0 with r3=A before return 1. Source-file storage must remain valid through this request, not merely through parser entry. The release descendants are unqueried.
sourceAllocationAndOwnership.releaseDispatch: 0x82D3D9F0 retains A, obtains a manager through 0x82D3DA78, and conditionally queries 0x82D2E3D0(manager+0x1080,A,outputCell) at 0x82D3DA24. A nonzero low-byte result selects 0x82D2E960 at 0x82D3DA40; the other arm calls 0x827F5780(A) at 0x82D3DA4C. Those children and allocator membership are unqueried.
sourceAllocationAndOwnership.resourceCleanupDistinction: 0x8258AED8 operates on resource/lock-state object slots, not a locally bound raw DDS allocation A. The height caller requests release through sub_82D3D9F0 on the two recorded exits; its sub_827F5780/sub_82D2E960 paths remain unqueried, so actual freeing and allocator compatibility are not asserted.
sourceAllocationAndOwnership.directAllocation: sub_82D38C80 samples L at 0x82D38CDC and, for nonzero L, requests low32(L+4) bytes through 0x82D3DBA0 at 0x82D38D00. It stores BE length L at A at 0x82D38D10, requests L bytes into A+4 through 0x82D38448 at 0x82D38D20, and requests release through 0x82D3D9F0(A) at 0x82D38D30 on a zero read-helper result. Both common-loader direct-return sites therefore use the same layout as the stream arm.
sourceAllocationAndOwnership.sharedCapacity: With nonwrapping L+4, ordinary allocator effects and retained valid storage, both direct and stream arms supply the requested L+4-byte block: four prefix bytes and L file bytes. This records the allocation request/capacity contract, not allocator rounding, successful complete delivery by 0x82D38448 or writability of the returned range; those remain premises.

replacementContract.recommendedMode: Equal-size in-place copying at 0x822D6508 is supported under the listed premises: confirmed caller, runtime-captured exact-name identity, nonnull allocation, replacement length==L, valid nonwrapping prefix/payload backing and writable guest range [A+4,A+4+L). Copy the complete DDS to A+4 while retaining r3=A and the BE prefix. This retains allocation identity and satisfies the observed r5 size consumer; it does not establish runtime safety or unread parser checks.
replacementContract.retailProfile: The observed candidate in xbox-heights-authoring-contract.json#/retailObservedProfile is a 524416-byte complete heights DDS. Use that size only after validating both the intended donor and the current prefix; it is not a mandatory-size theorem. This candidate does not close authored sample values, scale, dimensions or runtime acceptance.
replacementContract.donorLifetime: A separately retained donor buffer can serve only as the copy source and must remain valid through copy completion. The destination remains the native file allocation. A host source buffer is not itself a guest pointer replacement.
replacementContract.pointerSubstitution: If replacing r3 instead, supply a compatible guest allocation A_new with valid 4+L_new backing, BE U32[A_new]=L_new and complete DDS bytes at A_new+4. Native code derives P_new and requests release through sub_82D3D9F0(A_new). Account for displaced A through its compatible release policy; overwriting r3 alone leaves that allocation unaccounted for. Actual free-path effects and compatibility remain open.
replacementContract.systemHeapRuling: The logo's never-freed SystemHeapAlloc pointer pattern is not a corroborated splice at this site. The native height success and creation-failure paths still request release through sub_82D3D9F0 for the substituted base. Effects of sub_827F5780/sub_82D2E960 and allocator compatibility are unqueried; a never-freed lifetime cannot be assumed. A borrowed pointer without the BE prefix also violates the local layout.

nativeByteTransfer.localHandoff: The selected post-load wrapper/height/getter instructions publish pointers and length/context fields, not a sample-pair conversion. Retention through ordinary helpers remains required. Reuse the selected DDS parser/copy/extraction facts in xbox-dds-map-role-texture-contract.json; they do not establish complete file-to-CPU byte identity.
nativeByteTransfer.localResourceResult: Complete selected bodies 0x8269A238, 0x8269A160 and 0x8258AED8 contain no direct payload-pair swap, byte-reversed load/store, pixel loop or pixel-byte copy. Their child effects and resource generation still gate a byte-order claim.
nativeByteTransfer.lockPublication: 0x8269A238 calls 0x8269A160 at 0x8269A268 and publishes returned pitch and pointer to output+0/+4 at 0x8269A2B8/0x8269A2BC. An optional offset record adjusts the pointer. Neither pointer publication nor format-bit arithmetic proves it is the original source-payload storage.
lockFrontiers: 0x8269A1B8 -> 0x82699C98: resource/level inputs and output cells are delegated; this is the first unclosed child effect in the reached lock child.
0x8269A1CC -> 0x82698FC8: a format-index-derived factor feeds pitch metadata; child effects remain open.

0x8269A21C -> 0x82697CA0: resource, sampled page fields, offset and flags reach an opaque child. Its returned pointer plus a fresh offset is published at 0x8269A220..0x8269A228. Actual backing, representation and resource identity remain open.
cleanupFrontiers: 0x8258AEF0..0x8258AF08 -> 0x82698FB0: input is sampled object+8 if nonzero, otherwise sampled object+4 if nonzero. The helper's effects are not accepted here.

0x8258AF5C -> 0x8258ADF0: reached only after fresh object+4,+8,+16 nonzero tests and bit0 of object+0 clear. After intervening 0x821D5678 requests, r3/r4 reload object+8/+4. Copy-back or byte effects remain open; incoming flags0 does not prove these fields zero.

0x8258AF78/0x8258AF8C/0x8258AFB4 -> 0x826981D8 receives nonzero current object+8/+12/+4; 0x8258AFA0 -> 0x8268CE38 receives nonzero object+16. Local slot clearing does not establish the helpers' payload or allocation effects.
nativeByteTransfer.composition: Selected upload cleanup precedes the later height extraction under the existing creation chain. A same-resource, same-level-0, same-generation join through the opaque helpers is still required. Retail-observed LE16 file samples and unsigned BE16 CPU consumption remain separate facts; the native transfer is not closed.

currentEvidence.method: Serialized foreground read-only function queries and selected native-word reads from the supported program, comparison with the pinned flat image, raw operand/branch decoding and clipped exact-owner generated corroboration. Truncated decompiler output was not used as complete-body evidence. Exact generated direct-call/LR enumeration and a bounded direct-opener read corroborate the source-arm capacity and coverage qualifications.
currentEvidence.qualification: The initial 411 and additional 73 selected native query words matched the pinned image. This is selected-word equality, not whole-database identity or a runtime result. Generated caller enumeration is corroborated at its direct branch sites; indirect callers and upstream warm-bypass behavior remain unknown. Known thunk repairs/truncation do not establish unqueried helper effects. No project repair or runtime execution was performed.

unresolved: Allocator rounding/effects, actual complete-read semantics of 0x82D38448 and the other selected read helper, writable backing and concrete source/provider identity; the direct/stream L+4 allocation layout itself is bound.
Exact runtime caller-built filename prefix/path/case after sub_827F2830, and warm bypass behavior in the three height callers; indirect wrapper/height callers remain unknown.
Parser-internal size checks beyond the selected creation handoff window; equal-size copying satisfies only the observed r5=BE U32[P-4] consumer.
Compatibility of arbitrary replacement allocations with the current manager/fallback release path, and safe invocation of the native allocator from a host hook.
Getter/current-global and other opaque-helper alias effects and retention of the same filename, file allocation and creation context.
Native file-to-CPU sample transfer through parser/conversion conditions, the listed resource lock/cleanup children and the same-resource/level-0 generation join.
Successful runtime hook reachability, authored DDS acceptance, world/sample joins and actual TerrainZScale delivery.
guards: Apply scope.qualification to every corroborated static tuple. The hook remains a candidate; this is not implementation or runtime proof.
At the candidate hook r3 is prefix allocation A, not DDS pointer P. The wrapper adds four; the height caller derives A=P-4 for its release request.
Keep the BE32 allocation-length prefix, little-endian DDS header and unresolved sample-byte transfer separate.
Use the saved caller and runtime-captured complete intended filename; preserve load failure and the other enumerated wrapper consumers.
An equal-size copy is supported only under the listed backing, writability, alias, helper and arithmetic premises. The observed r5 length consumer is not an exhaustive parser-size contract.
Describe sub_82D3D9F0 as a release request while its free paths are unqueried. Resource cleanup and scalar-deleting object release do not bind raw DDS freeing or sample swapping.
Do not infer SystemHeapAlloc compatibility, successful full read, helper retention or a closed LE16-to-BE16 transfer from local pointer arithmetic or memcpy.
conclusion: 0x822D6508 has a corroborated static candidate tuple for the cited numbered/named height route, with unique direct-caller LR 0x822F98BC. Both direct and stream source arms request L+4 prefix/payload storage. Equal-size copying into A+4 is supported under the listed premises and satisfies the observed r5 size consumer. Exact filename identity requires runtime capture; free-path compatibility, unread parser checks and the LE16-to-BE16 transfer remain open.
